classification.difficultyReason: Infer the triangle's base and perpendicular height from the circle's radius, then subtract its area from the circle's area.

content.prompt: A triangle is inscribed in a circle, as shown. Calculate the shaded area to 2 d.p.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 9 diagram below the prompt, on the left
spec.description: A circle with an inscribed triangle whose base is a horizontal diameter and whose apex is the topmost point. The dashed perpendicular altitude meets the marked centre, with a right-angle marker above the diameter. The region outside the triangle and inside the circle is shaded. The radius label is below the diameter toward the right.
spec.mathematics: The radius is 12.5 cm. The triangle's base is the diameter, 25 cm, and its perpendicular height is the radius, 12.5 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: The given radius and measured-region shading remain visible; no calculated lengths or areas are printed in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
The triangle's base is the diameter, $25\text{ cm}$, and its perpendicular height is $12.5\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}
A_1 &= \pi(12.5)^2\\
A_1 &= 156.25\pi\text{ cm}^2\\
A_2 &= \frac12(25)(12.5)\\
A_2 &= 156.25\text{ cm}^2\\
A_{\text{Total}} &= A_1-A_2\\
A_{\text{Total}} &= (156.25\pi-156.25)\text{ cm}^2\\
A_{\text{Total}} &\approx 334.62\text{ cm}^2
\end{align*}$$
